info.desc: Meteora is the second studio album by American rock band Linkin Park, released on March 25th, 2003. Following the collaboration album Reanimation which featured remixes of their debut album Hybrid Theory. Linkin Park released singles from Meteora for over a year, including "Somewhere I Belong", "Faint", "Lying from You", "From the Inside", "Breaking the Habit" and "Numb". It is the most successful album in the history of the Modern Rock Tracks chart, a chart that specializes in radio play of alternative rock songs. "Numb" was the biggest song of the year on the chart. podcast.body: Released in the spring of 2003, Meteora was considered a "difficult second album" but achieved commercial success comparable to Hybrid Theory, selling 27 million copies worldwide by 2003 despite the prevalence of illegal file sharing. The band demoed at least 80 different songs for it over an eight-month period while constantly on tour, resulting in a tight collection of 13 tracks under 37 minutes. "Mediaora was as big a hit as Hybrid 3."

podcast.body: Released on March 25, 2003, this second studio album was titled after monasteries in a region of Greece. It was a challenging follow-up, with producer Don Gilmore pushing the band, including making them work on 40 different choruses for its first single. Within a week, it sold over 810,000 copies in the US alone, reaching nearly 6 million in America, 500,000 in Canada, and 250,000 in Australia. Worldwide, sales totaled around 13 million copies, even as the recording industry faced a collapse in CD sales due to file sharing. "Meteora, the second Lincoln Park album was released on March 25th of 2003, and within a week it sold more than 810,000 copies in the US alone."
